system_description.narrative_title: Nvidia CEO spy-affair and the destabilisation of the AI-finance-geopolitics nexus
system_description.narrative_summary: A scandal around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — an admitted affair with a woman alleged to be linked to Chinese intelligence — has propagated through markets, regulators, corporate governance, and US–China tech policy, creating cascading shocks across the AI industry. Treated as an open system, the episode admits inflows (intelligence allegations, capital reallocations, regulatory scrutiny, media coverage) and outflows (stock volatility, policy proposals, board actions, supply‑chain re‑routing), with reinforcing feedbacks between investor sentiment, legislative pressure, and corporate responses that amplify uncertainty. The same dynamics interact with concurrent high‑stakes capital events (notably Anthropic's jumbo IPO) so that reputational, financial and geopolitical signals cross‑feed one another, raising systemic fragility in the AI and semiconductor ecosystem.
system_description.scope: Inside the system: Nvidia (CEO, board, employees), major AI firms (Anthropic, OpenAI, CoreWeave, others), global investors and markets, US and allied regulators and lawmakers, China-linked actors and supply‑chain nodes (Singapore, Taiwan, Chinese universities), semiconductor manufacturers and trade channels, and media/governance institutions influencing public signal flows.
system_description.super_system: The global techno‑economic‑geopolitical system centered on AI and semiconductors — i.e., the international AI-industrial-financial system shaped by cross-border trade, national security policy, and capital markets.
adjacent_subsystems: Global capital markets & IPO ecosystem (bankers, retail/ institutional investors, valuation formation)
US–China geopolitical and trade policy apparatus (export controls, congressional oversight, diplomacy)
Semiconductor manufacturing & supply chain (TSMC, Singapore hubs, chip export routes)
AI research & commercialization ecosystem (model developers, cloud providers, data‑centre infrastructure)

variables.name: Investor sentiment toward AI markets
variables.description: Average market confidence and risk appetite among investors for AI‑related assets and companies.

variables.name: Equity market volatility
variables.description: Short‑to‑medium‑term magnitude of price fluctuations across equities relevant to the AI‑semiconductor ecosystem.

variables.name: Regulatory scrutiny of technology transfers
variables.description: Intensity and scope of regulatory attention and oversight applied to cross‑border technology transfers and exports.

variables.name: Corporate governance integrity
variables.description: Degree of board independence, disclosure quality and internal control robustness within major technology firms.

variables.name: Key‑person dependency risk
variables.description: Extent to which organisational performance and strategic continuity depend on one or a few individual leaders.

variables.name: Capital allocation into AI sector
variables.description: Net financial flows (equity, debt, and private financing) directed into AI infrastructure, platforms, and firms over time.

variables.name: Valuation bubble pressure
variables.description: Degree to which asset prices in the AI and semiconductor space exceed fundamentals and are driven by momentum or hype.

variables.name: Geopolitical tension over technology
variables.description: Level of interstate strategic friction and policy conflict related to advanced technology competition and control.

variables.name: Semiconductor supply‑chain resilience
variables.description: Ability of semiconductor production and logistics networks to absorb shocks and maintain output and delivery.

variables.name: Media coverage intensity
variables.description: Volume and prominence of media reporting and investigative attention focused on actors and events in the ecosystem.

variables.name: Investor market liquidity
variables.description: Availability of tradable capital and depth in markets that determine how easily positions in AI‑related assets can be entered or exited.

variables.name: Momentum of regulatory policy change
variables.description: Rate at which new laws, rules or administrative actions affecting technology trade and governance are being proposed and advanced.

variables.name: Legal liability and disclosure risk
variables.description: Aggregate probability and expected severity of legal claims, enforcement actions or disclosure shortfalls impacting firms in the system.

variables.name: Capital flow controls
variables.description: Degree of policy‑imposed restrictions or barriers on cross‑border financial movements and investments into technology assets.

variables.name: Skilled talent mobility
variables.description: Fluidity of movement for skilled technical workers and researchers across organisations and national borders.

variables.name: Trust in international technical collaboration
variables.description: Perceived reliability and security of cross‑border research, partnerships and information sharing between technical actors.

catalysts.title: Nvidia board decision on Jensen Huang
catalysts.description: Board meeting to decide Huang's future — possible ouster, retention or negotiated departure that will crystallise corporate direction and market confidence.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia board meets to decide CEO Huang's future'; 'Nvidia prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang' — board action will be decisive.

catalysts.title: Possible Congressional testimony / subpoena of Jensen Huang
catalysts.description: Lawmakers push to summon Huang; testimony or subpoena could trigger oversight, disclosures and policy responses affecting tech governance and geopolitics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US lawmakers summon Jensen Huang'; 'House Republicans push for Huang to testify, float subpoena'.

catalysts.title: Anthropic IPO trading debut (planned Nov 19, 2026)
catalysts.description: Anthropic aims to start trading Nov. 19 at a record valuation, a major liquidity and sentiment event for the AI market and capital allocation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Anthropic to start trading Nov. 19'; 'Anthropic IPO targeting $1.3–1.5tn valuation'.

catalysts.title: U.S. commerce decision on Megaspeed blacklist inclusion
catalysts.description: Commerce Department's pending decision whether to include Singapore-based Megaspeed on export blacklist, affecting trade and enforcement precedents.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US commerce department delays Megaspeed’s inclusion on trade blacklist'; 'What we know about Megaspeed'.

catalysts.title: Wachtell Lipton-led internal investigation at Nvidia
catalysts.description: Independent probe into CEO affair and disclosures will continue, shaping governance reforms, filings and legal exposures over months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia hires Wachtell Lipton to lead probe'; 'Meet the former prosecutor Nvidia hired to investigate the scandal'.

catalysts.title: Lawsuits and disclosure litigation against Nvidia and Huang
catalysts.description: Existing suits and new filings over disclosures and liability will proceed, increasing legal risk and investor uncertainty over coming months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia, CEO Huang sued'; 'Could Huang, Nvidia and company's board be held liable over affair scandal?'.

catalysts.title: Momentum for U.S. laws tightening AI chip access to China
catalysts.description: Lawmakers are pushing new chip-restriction proposals that could accelerate legislative or regulatory barriers on advanced AI semiconductor exports.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia spy allegations likely to spur laws to tighten China's access to AI chips'; 'US lawmakers push China chip rules'.

catalysts.title: TSMC investment into Anthropic/OpenAI
catalysts.description: TSMC's approved plan to invest up to $1bn into Anthropic and OpenAI will channel industry capital and deepen chip-AI firm ties.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'TSMC to invest up to $1 billion in Anthropic, OpenAI' — triggers capital flows and tighter industry links.
